items.text: Corrections to the previous lecture
$\Delta$: categories with arbitrary small inverse limits. Problem 1: $C$ small, envelope:
C\hookrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C,\mathbf{Sets})^{\circ}\qquad(\text{fully faithful, } c\mapsto h_c)
Problem 2: $E\in\Delta$, $\Sigma$ small set of arrows: universal $\Delta$-functor inverting $\Sigma$.
\tilde\Sigma=\text{saturation of }\Sigma;\qquad E[\tilde\Sigma^{-1}]
Error 1. $\tilde\Sigma$ is never small; the Homs of $E[\tilde\Sigma^{-1}]$ need not be small sets.
\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)=\varinjlim_{X_i\to X\,\in\tilde\Sigma}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i,Y)\quad\text{(indexing category may be large)}
If there is a solution it is this one; but it may be too large. So only an idea of proof.
Error 2. « An algebraic theory is built in two steps; $I$ strictly cogenerates $R$. » False already for one base element.
Groups on one base element: endomorphisms of it are only the $n$-th power maps, which do not determine the group structure.
The mistake: « strictly (co)generating » is not transitive.
C\subset C'\subset C »,\ C\ \text{strictly gen. in } C',\ C'\ \text{in } C »\ \not\Rightarrow\ C\ \text{in } C »
\mathbf{Gp}:\ \mathbb Z\ \text{strictly generates the free groups}\ \bigl(F=\textstyle\coprod\mathbb Z\bigr);\ \text{free groups generate } \mathbf{Gp}

Every group is an effective quotient of a free group (generators and relations). But $\mathbb Z$ does not strictly generate $\mathbf{Gp}$; that would say a group structure is determined by power maps.
So a long transfinite construction may be needed (a small one, ending at a small ordinal).
Error 3: the criterion
R\in\Delta\ \text{algebraic}\ \overset{\text{claimed}}{\iff}\ R\ \text{has a small strictly cogenerating family}\qquad(\Rightarrow\ \text{true, }\Leftarrow\ \text{false})
Counterexample: $R=\mathbf{Sets}^{\circ}$, with strict cogenerator the two-element set; yet $R$ is not algebraic.
The condition needed is stronger: accessibility (SGA 4, I, § 9, revised).
Discussion: is $\mathbf{Sets}^{\circ}$ algebraic?
From the room: $\mathbf{Sets}^{\circ}\simeq$ complete atomic Boolean algebras.
E\mapsto 2^E=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Sets}}(E,I_2)\ \ (\text{subsets of }E),\qquad I_2=\{0,1\}
The structure: infinite unions, infinite intersections, distributivity, complement $X\mapsto X'$, bottom and top elements.
X\cap\bigcup_i Y_i=\bigcup_i (X\cap Y_i)\qquad X\cap X'=\varnothing,\ \ X\cup X'=E
Complement as extra data $X\mapsto X'$, axioms on it.
Problem: « for every set $I$ » is not one axiom but a family of axioms — not small.
Algebraic structures here: a small set of data and axioms at each step; « for every indexing set » is large.
(Room) The right duality is with Stone spaces (zero-dimensional); not needed.
Not a question of truth but of the set-up: a notion where representing theories by universal structures works.
For each cardinal there are ordered sets with distributivity up to $\pi$ but not for all index sets.
Challenge: give a small set of axioms for complete atomic Boolean algebras. None offered.
Even one family of operations indexed by all sets $I$ is non-small.
(Room) quantifying over sets is second order; or infinitary universal algebra with a non-small set of operations.
For a fixed set $I$: one composition law, fine. Not a non-small set of laws in the data.
Reply: bounding by the cardinality of $X$ makes it depend on $X$; axioms must not.
Each Boolean algebra fits a $\pi$-Boolean theory; the theory itself is intermediate between algebraic and e.g. topological spaces.
Reduction to $\Delta_\pi$
\Delta_\pi=\text{categories with inverse limits indexed by } |\mathrm{Ar}|\le\pi
Algebraic theories in $\Delta_\pi$ are small categories; those of $\Delta$: the $\Delta$-envelope (add arbitrary inverse limits) of a small object of $\Delta_\pi$.
These are the accessible (or co-accessible) categories: $R$ carries the universal object, $S=R^\circ$ the set realisations.
Definitions (accessibility)
1. An ordered (or preordered) set $I$ is $\pi$-dominating if filtering and
\forall(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\subset I,\ |\Lambda|\le\pi\ \ \exists x\in I:\ x\ge x_\alpha\ \forall\alpha
For $\pi\ge2$ this implies filtering; $\pi=2$ is exactly filtering. We take $\pi$ infinite.
2. $E$ satisfies condition $L_\pi$:
(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}\ \text{direct system},\ I\ \pi\text{-dominating, small}\ \Longrightarrow\ \varinjlim x_\alpha\ \text{exists in } E
$E$ satisfies $L$ if $L_\pi$ holds for some small $\pi$.
3. $F\colon E\to E'$ is $\pi$-accessible if $E$ satisfies $L_\pi$ and $F$ commutes with direct limits indexed by $\pi$-dominating $I$.
Accessible: $\pi$-accessible for some small $\pi$.
For large categories, a good functor behaves well with direct limits (large) or with inverse limits; if neither, it is out of reach — the next universe.
4. An object $X$ of $E$ is $\pi$-accessible if the covariant functor
h_X=\operatorname{Hom}(X,-)\colon E\to\mathbf{Sets}\quad\text{is } \pi\text{-accessible}
$X$ accessible if $\pi$-accessible for some small $\pi$.
5. $E$ is $\pi$-accessible if there is a small full subcategory $C\subset E$, strictly generating (every object a direct limit of a diagram in $C$), with all objects of $C$ accessible.
$E$ accessible if $\pi$-accessible for some small $\pi$.
1–4 are in SGA 4, I; 5 differs (SGA had only a small generating category).
Propositions
$E$, $F$ satisfy $L_\pi$; $\operatorname{Hom}_\pi(E,F)\subset\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)$: the $\pi$-accessible functors.
(a) $\operatorname{Hom}_\pi$ is stable under direct limits that exist in $F$ (computed argumentwise): trivial.
\text{(b)}\ \ J\ \text{small},\ |\mathrm{Ar}\,J|\le\pi,\ \varprojlim_J\ \text{exists in } F\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}_\pi(E,F)\ \text{stable under } \varprojlim_J
Reduces to: $\pi$-dominating filtering direct limits commute with inverse limits of cardinality $\le\pi$ in $\mathbf{Sets}$.
Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{acc}}(E,F)$ is stable under direct limits and under small inverse limits computed argumentwise.
Corollaries for objects
$E_\pi$: the strictly full subcategory of $\pi$-accessible objects of $E$.
E_\pi\ \text{is stable under direct limits of type } J,\ |\mathrm{Ar}\,J|\le\pi
X=\varinjlim X_j\ \Rightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}(X,-)=\varprojlim_j\operatorname{Hom}(X_j,-)
Hence: if $E$ satisfies $L$, the accessible objects are stable under arbitrary (small) direct limits.
$E$ accessible $\Rightarrow$ every object of $E$ is accessible (a direct limit of objects of $C$).
Next: a criterion to find at least one accessible object.
